prompt: Given \(f(x) = 2 + \sqrt{x}\), what are the domain and range of \(f^{-1}(x)\)?
why: \(f\) has domain \(x \ge 0\) and range \(y \ge 2\). The inverse swaps them: domain \(x \ge 2\), range \(y \ge 0\).

prompt: Which of the following is an anti-derivative of \(\dfrac{1}{9x^2 + 1}\)?
why: \(\frac{1}{9x^2 + 1} = \frac{1}{1 + (3x)^2}\). Differentiating \(\tan^{-1}(3x)\) gives \(\frac{3}{1 + 9x^2}\), so divide by 3: \(\frac{1}{3}\tan^{-1}(3x) + c\).

prompt: Sam starts at the origin and walks along all of the vector \(3\underset{\sim}{i} + \underset{\sim}{j}\), then all of \(-\underset{\sim}{i} + 4\underset{\sim}{j}\), and finally all of \(2\underset{\sim}{i} - 2\underset{\sim}{j}\). How far from the origin is Sam?
why: Add the vectors to get the final position: \((3 - 1 + 2)\underset{\sim}{i} + (1 + 4 - 2)\underset{\sim}{j} = 4\underset{\sim}{i} + 3\underset{\sim}{j}\), which is \(\sqrt{16 + 9} = 5\) from the origin. Adding the three lengths gives the distance walked, not the distance from the start.

prompt: A monic polynomial \(p(x)\) of degree 4 has a zero of multiplicity 2 at \(x = -1\) and is divisible by \(x^2 - 2x + 3\). Which of the following could be the graph of \(p(x)\)?
why: \(p(x) = (x + 1)^2(x^2 - 2x + 3)\). The quadratic has discriminant \(4 - 12 < 0\), so it is always positive and gives no more \(x\)-intercepts. So the graph only touches the \(x\)-axis at \(x = -1\), is never negative, and (monic, even degree) rises on both ends.

why: Choose the seven finalists: \(\binom{12}{7} = \frac{12!}{7!\,5!}\). Then fill 1st, 2nd and 3rd from them in order: \(7 \times 6 \times 5 = \frac{7!}{4!}\). Multiplying, the \(7!\) cancels: \(\frac{12!}{5!\,4!}\).

why: The foot of the perpendicular from \((5, 5)\) to the line is \((2, 6)\), the midpoint of the point and its reflection. So \(\overrightarrow{OA} = 2\begin{pmatrix} 2 \\ 6 \end{pmatrix} - \begin{pmatrix} 5 \\ 5 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} -1 \\ 7 \end{pmatrix}\).

= 2\cos^3\theta - \cos\theta - 2(1 - \cos^2\theta)\cos\theta = 4\cos^3\theta - 3\cos\theta. Dividing by 4 and rearranging gives the result.
(ii) 8\cos^3\theta - 6\cos\theta + 1 = 0, so 2(4\cos^3\theta - 3\cos\theta) = -1, that is 2\cos 3\theta = -1 and \cos 3\theta = -\frac{1}{2}.
(iii) 3\theta = \frac{2\pi}{3}, \frac{4\pi}{3}, \frac{8\pi}{3} give \theta = \frac{2\pi}{9}, \frac{4\pi}{9}, \frac{8\pi}{9}. Their cosines are all different, so the three roots of the cubic are 2\cos\frac{2\pi}{9}, 2\cos\frac{4\pi}{9}, 2\cos\frac{8\pi}{9}.
For x^3 - 3x + 1 = 0: \sum\alpha = 0 and \sum\alpha\beta = -3, so \sum\alpha^2 = 0^2 - 2(-3) = 6.
4\left(\cos^2\frac{2\pi}{9} + \cos^2\frac{4\pi}{9} + \cos^2\frac{8\pi}{9}\right) = 6, so the sum is \frac{3}{2}.
